title: Keys and scales, the short version
summary: The 7 notes of a key, why trap lives in minor, and scale lock as training wheels.

steps.title: A key is seven notes
steps.body:
A **key** is a set of seven notes that sound right together, with one of them as home. **A minor** is A B C D E F G: every white key on the piano, with A as home.

Stay inside those seven notes and your melody, chords and 808 agree with each other. Step outside and you hear a rub. Sometimes that's spice; usually it's a mistake.

Minor keys sound dark and tense. Major keys sound bright. That's why most trap, cloud rap and UG beats sit in minor: the mood is the music.
steps.deeper:
A scale is a pattern of **whole steps** (W, 2 half steps) and **half steps** (H, 1 half step).

**Natural minor** is W H W W H W W: A→B (W), B→C (H), C→D (W), D→E (W), E→F (H), F→G (W), G→A (W).

**Major** is W W H W W W H. In A: A B C# D E F# G#.

Number the notes 1 to 7 up from home. These are **scale degrees**, and the in-app keyboard shows them on each key.

C major uses the same seven notes as A minor. What changes is which note feels like home. Keys that share notes like this are called **relative** major and minor.

steps.title: Minor vs major, note by note
steps.caption: The same run up and down over the same drums and 808. Only the 3rd, 6th and 7th notes change.

examples.label: A natural minor
examples.explanation: A B C D E F G. Dark, a little sad. Home turf for trap.

examples.label: A major
examples.explanation: A B C# D E F# G#. Same home note, three notes raised a half step. Now it sounds bright and sunny.

steps.title: Flavors of minor
steps.body:
Minor comes in flavors. Two you'll hear all the time in beats:

**Harmonic minor** raises the 7th note: in A minor, G becomes G#. That one note adds a dramatic, eerie pull back to home.

**Minor pentatonic** keeps just five notes: A C D E G. No two of them are a half step apart, so nothing rubs. That's why noodling in it sounds good fast.

In the app, **scale lock** fades out every key outside your track's key so you can't hit a wrong note. Treat it as training wheels: use it until your ear knows the way.
steps.deeper:
**Harmonic minor**: 1 2 b3 4 5 b6 7. In A: A B C D E F G#. The jump from F to G# is 3 half steps (an **augmented second**), which gives it that exotic, dark sound. G# sits a half step below A, so it pulls hard toward home. It also turns the minor v chord (Em) into a major V chord (E), which pulls strongly back to Am.

**Minor pentatonic**: 1 b3 4 5 b7. In A: A C D E G. It drops the 2nd and 6th (B and F) from natural minor.

Scale lock and this lesson's check both use natural minor (or major, in a major key). A G# counts as outside A minor here, but every pentatonic note is inside it.

steps.title: Three minor flavors
steps.caption: Same drums, same 808 on A, and the same phrase each time with one or two notes swapped. Listen to the last notes of bar 2.

examples.label: A natural minor
examples.explanation: A B C D E F G. The phrase ends with a whole step up from G to A: settled and moody.

examples.label: A harmonic minor
examples.explanation: One change: G becomes G#. Now the last step up into A is a half step, and it pulls home hard. Darker, more dramatic.

examples.label: A minor pentatonic
examples.explanation: Only A C D E G. F and B are swapped out for G and A. Smoother and more open, with nothing rubbing.

steps.title: Four notes, all in key
steps.prompt:
Turn on **Scale lock** (the switch just above the keys). Now every key you can play is in your track's key.

Write a melody with **at least 4 notes**: tap **Record from keyboard** and play, or tap cells in the piano roll. Press play to hear it loop.
hints: Scale lock only guards the keyboard. Notes you tap into the piano roll can land outside the key. In-key rows are tinted, and out-of-key note names are greyed out.
The keys marked **1** are home. Try degrees 1, 3, 5, 3 (in A minor that's A, C, E, C): four notes that can't miss.
If the check names a note outside your key, tap it in the piano roll to remove it, then tap the row just above or below it instead. In a major or natural minor key, both of those are in key.

steps.message: That was a practice rep, so nothing goes into Your Track yet. You'll write the melody you keep in the next stage, The idea.
